Max Chen: Quick Q — if the regional runtime falls back to a secondary region (active/active), what guarantee do we have that tenant data doesn't leave the primary region? Need clarity for EU/PDPA customers.

Priya Patel: Short answer: none unless we enforce residency at the proxy/orchestrator layer. Our current fallback path will forward to any compatible region.

Sam Ortiz: We mentioned this in the original RFC but never settled on a fallback contract. Options I remember: (1) strict local-only rejects fallback, (2) guarded fallback for stateless ops, (3) escrowed payload handoff with ephemeral encryption keys.

Andrea Gomez: +1 to guarded fallback for latency-sensitive reads. Writes are trickier — should be reject or escrow only.

Max Chen: For guarded fallback, how do we detect "stateless"? Proposal: tenant metadata + request header `X-Residency-Policy: local-only|escrow|anywhere` so proxy can make decisions.

Sam Ortiz: Header is okay but must be authoritative server-side. Clients can lie. Enforcement must consult tenant config in control plane before routing.

Priya Patel: We also need an immutable audit trail if we ever forward outside tenant region. Legal wants proof.

Sam Ortiz: Prototype handshake pseudocode I sketched: 
```
if tenant.residency == "EU" and target.region != tenant.region:
  if tenant.policy == "local-only":
    return 403
  if tenant.policy == "escrow":
    ephemeral_key = kms.rotate_ephemeral_key()
    encrypted_payload = encrypt(payload, ephemeral_key)
    store_claim(encrypted_payload, meta)
    forward_to_secondary(encrypted_payload, key_ref=ephemeral_key.ref)
```

Andrea Gomez: Perf note: encrypting + decrypting on handoff adds ~2-5ms with hardware accel, more on CPU paths. Tradeoff between privacy and tail latency.

Max Chen: For SLA tiers: premium customers get guaranteed local-only (we can reserve capacity), mid-tier can opt into escrow, free-tier default is anywhere. That maps to pricing and contracts.

deploy-bot: [canary] rollout: `fallback-policy-v2` deployed to staging at 2024-08-15T09:12:00Z :rocket: 

Priya Patel: Operational changes: update routing docs, add `fallback_residency_reason` tag to telemetry, and add runbook step to manually disable cross-region fallback per-tenant.

Sam Ortiz: Action items: (1) tenant metadata + header enforcement (Priya) (2) escrow handshake prototype + KMS flow (Sam) (3) perf/stress tests in staging (Andrea) (4) docs & runbook updates (Max). I'll open the PRs and link.

Max Chen: SGTM. If someone can build the staging harness this week that'd be huge. :thumbsup:

Andrea Gomez: I'll stand up a load test job — target 10k req/s mixed-policy, measure p50/p95 tails and KMS latency impact.

Max Chen: Also, legal flagged retention: audit logs for fallback events must be immutable for 7 years. That impacts log storage/retention policy.

Priya Patel: Noted — will sync with security/legal on SLA wording.

Sam Ortiz: FWIW, we should include a "fallback_approval" boolean in tenant config so enterprise security can opt-in global fallback with manual approval.

Max Chen: Thanks all — I’ll follow up with PR links in this thread and assign owners. Linking RFC we referenced: https://redwood/infra/rfc/region-fallback-2024
